//: The TEST compile. `npm test` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node --test`, for the
same reason the daemon does (CLAUDE.md): compiling first type-checks the tests, and a
type error is a test failure rather than something a runner silently strips.
WHY commonjs HERE AND ESNext IN tsconfig.json. Vite consumes the sources directly and
resolves extensionless relative imports itself. Node does not: under ESM it requires a
file extension on every relative specifier, which would mean writing `./x.js` in TSX
that Vite then has to be taught to resolve back to `./x.tsx`. Emitting CommonJS for the
test run sidesteps that entirely — node resolves extensionless paths, `react/jsx-runtime`
resolves, and the SAME source files are checked and executed. This is also why
The consequence, stated so it is not rediscovered: `import.meta` is unavailable under
CommonJS, so no source file may use `import.meta.env`. Nothing needs it — the client is
same-origin with both services through the nginx proxy, so every request path is
relative and there is no base URL to inject.
